data.name: Adar
data.gender_notes: Adar is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘Adarah’ meaning ‘new beginnings’ or ‘rain’ which signifies a time of renewal and growth, often associated with the onset of spring. The name Adar carries the meaning “Spring, New Beginnings” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Adar usually hope their child will grow to embody spring, new beginnings and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the rebirth of nature and the renewal of one's spiritual and personal growth.
data.etymology: Adar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Spring, New Beginnings.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adar total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_urdu.name: عدار

in_english.name: Adar
in_english.meaning: Adar is the second month in the Hebrew calendar
in_english.long_meaning: Adar is the second month in the Hebrew calendar, it is a month in the Jewish year, and it is mentioned in the Quran. The name Adar has its roots in ancient Semitic languages and is associated with nobility and excellence. In Islamic tradition, the name Adar signifies a person of high moral character and spiritual distinction. Historically, Adar has been used as a given name among Jewish and Muslim communities, symbolizing a connection to their rich cultural heritage. The name Adar embodies qualities of leadership, wisdom, and compassion, making it a meaningful choice for parents seeking a name with deep historical and spiritual significance.

data.cultural_impact: In the Islamic lunar calendar, Adar is the seventh month and is known for various cultural traditions and festivals. The month is significant in many Islamic communities as it marks the onset of spring, a time for new beginnings and renewal. During this time, many Muslims focus on acts of charity, kindness, and seeking forgiveness.
data.spiritual_significance: Adar holds spiritual significance as it is believed in Islamic tradition that September 17 is the night of ‘Arafat’, the most blessed day in the Islamic year. On this day, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) delivered his final sermon to millions of pilgrims gathered at Mount Arafat in Saudi Arabia, emphasizing the unity of humanity in all aspects and reminding everybody to stay firm on their faith and righteousness. Thus, Adar is a reminder for spiritual growth, introspection and commitment towards faith and moral values.
